governance_scope: Post-R7.5.3 architecture-reset evidence only; R7.5.3 remains closed and this evidence does not authorize additional H2/H3 readmission remediation.

advantage_memory.interpretation: Advantage memory is saturated, but the retained fraction is about 31-32%, materially less severe than the Strategy-memory truncation previously disproven as the primary cause. Capacity remains a secondary candidate, not the first causal remedy.

interpretation: HYP-B chance/return target noise receives strong evidence: even shared exact infosets have about 0.568 mean target-derived regret-matching TV and about 48.5% legal-slot sign disagreement.

HYP-C trajectory-feedback divergence also receives strong evidence: generated Advantage-sample count divergence grows from about 0.9% in iteration 1 to 21.6% in iteration 3, while the final Advantage networks disagree by about 0.51 behavior-policy TV on the same heldout states.
The very small marginal distribution TVs by street/legal/history length show that the problem is not a simple gross distribution imbalance; it is fine-grained support/target divergence.

HYP-D representation fragmentation is an amplifier because coarse geometry/history projections recover much more support overlap, but coarse target-derived policy TV remains about 0.54-0.57, so compression alone cannot be expected to cure the instability.
HYP-A Advantage-memory pressure remains plausible but is not yet causally isolated and is not the first remedy because target disagreement is already severe on shared exact infosets.

The next step should screen a variance-to-policy feedback remedy before any heavy retraining: average the ensemble raw Advantage estimates before the discontinuous regret-matching transform, while preserving the existing uncertainty-damping epsilon, and compare it read-only against the frozen current algebra.
